sections.title: Why Lakebase
sections.summary: Application teams struggle to choose, provision, scale and govern operational databases, especially across dev, test and production. Lakebase answers with serverless Postgres that separates compute from storage and lives inside the Data Intelligence Platform.
takeaways: Apps have become stateless, serverless and intelligent; databases have not kept pace
Separating compute from storage is what enables branching, scale to zero and fast recovery
Lower total cost comes from one governed platform, elastic compute and a better developer workflow

sections.title: Core capabilities
sections.summary: Five capabilities change how teams build on Postgres: instant zero-copy branches, point-in-time recovery, autoscaling, scale to zero, and read capacity that scales independently of writes.
takeaways: Branches give every developer or CI run an isolated copy without duplicating storage
Restore to an exact moment, and validate on a branch before touching production
Compute follows demand and suspends when idle, so you pay for active use

slides.title: What Lakebase is not for
slides.expectTitle: What should you NOT do with Lakebase?
slides.text:
Large scale migrations. For customers considering PostgreSQL migration → use Lakegate to assess readiness before committing (16 automated checks, readiness score, phased migration playbook)
Migration from non-postgres databases (Especially true for GraphQL and NoSQL DBs!)
Run workloads which require more than:
4000 concurrent connections (1000 for Lakebase provisioned)
16TB of Storage
Run OLAP workloads in an OLTP database, expecting improved performances (it won’t)
Splitting a large dataset into multiple branches or projects to workaround those restrictions is strongly discouraged
slides.note: The 1,000-connection figure for Lakebase Provisioned no longer applies: Provisioned has been retired and migrated to Autoscaling, where the limit is 4,000 concurrent connections.

sections.title: Autoscaling deep dive
sections.summary: A look under the hood: stateless computes in front of multi-tenant storage made of safekeepers, pageservers and object storage, spread across availability zones for resilience.
takeaways: Writes are persisted to three safekeepers before they are acknowledged
Pages are served from pageservers and reconstructed from object storage when needed
Three availability zones and a standby pageserver give built-in redundancy

slides.title: Storage high availability
slides.text:

X

Each Postgres instance uses 3 safekeepers located in different AZs. If one Safekeeper or AZ fails, the system can still reach consensus. Built-in redundancy. Immediate recovery.
Each Postgres instance is hosted on two pageservers: one active node and one secondary failover node, both nodes being located in different AZs. If a Pageserver fails, reads are automatically routed to the secondary failover node. Recovery in a few seconds.
Object storage has built-in multi-AZ redundancy. Immediate recovery.
